tasks.title: Your first list
tasks.statement: Create a list of the numbers 10, 20, 30. Add 40 to the end with the append method, replace the first element with 99, and print the whole list. You should get [99, 20, 30, 40].
tasks.starter:
nums = [10, 20, 30]
# append, assignment by index, print

tasks.title: First and last
tasks.statement: Write a function first_last(nums) that returns a list of two elements: the first and the last element of nums. The list is not empty. Use a negative index for the last one.
tasks.hint: return [nums[0], nums[-1]]. For a one-element list both indexes point to the same element.

tasks.title: Sum of a list
tasks.statement: Write a function total(nums): the sum of all elements of the list. For an empty list, return 0. Compute it with a loop and an accumulator, without the built-in sum function.
tasks.hint: for x in nums: result += x. It is the same accumulator as in the chapter on loops.

tasks.title: The largest element
tasks.statement: Write a function biggest(nums): the largest element of a non-empty list. Do not use the built-in max. Hint: start not from zero but from the first element, otherwise a list of only negative numbers will give a wrong answer.
tasks.hint: for x in nums: if x > best: best = x.
tasks.starter:
def biggest(nums):
    best = nums[0]
    # compare every element with best
    return best

tasks.title: How many above the limit
tasks.statement: Write a function count_greater(nums, limit): how many elements of the list are strictly greater than limit.
tasks.hint: A counter starting from zero; if x > limit: count += 1.

tasks.title: Pick the even ones
tasks.statement: Write a function evens(nums) that returns a NEW list of the even elements of nums in their original order. Create an empty list and fill it with append.

tasks.title: List of squares
tasks.statement: Write a function squares(nums): a new list in which each element is the square of the corresponding element of nums.
tasks.hint: result.append(x * x) on every pass of the loop.

tasks.title: Arithmetic mean
tasks.statement: Write a function average(nums): the arithmetic mean of a non-empty list, that is, the sum divided by the number of elements. The result is ordinary division (a float).
tasks.hint: return sum(nums) / len(nums). The built-in sum and len are fine here.

tasks.title: List without a value
tasks.statement: Write a function without(nums, x): a new list with all elements of nums except those equal to x (remove all occurrences, not just the first). The original order is preserved.
tasks.hint: Do not delete from the original list, fill a new one: if item != x: result.append(item).
